answer: To resist sybil attacks, each agent must emit a unique cryptographic pulse every epoch, hashed against a shared quartz reference crystal that stabilizes the network time. Peers then refract this pulse through a prism of independent attestations, requiring majority agreement before the identity is credited. An attacker forging many identities faces linear cost: each fake needs its own continuous pulse computation and risks inconsistent refraction patterns that the prism rejects, making mass sybil creation economically prohibitive.
